author: Chris Vetter
title: Sex offender, former pastor, enters plea to violating registration rules - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Vetter ,
8 hours ago
CHIPPEWA FALLS — A former pastor who served an 18-month prison sentence after he sexually assaulted a boy he met online has now entered a plea to violating his sex offender registration status.
Ervin S. Witmer, 64, of Withee entered a guilty plea Tuesday in Chippewa County Court to one count of sex registry violation.
Witmer also has been charged in Clark County Court with being a sex offender while working with children, which is a felony. He is due back in that court on July 29.
Judge James Isaacson accepted the plea and set sentencing for Oct. 6.
Witmer remains free on a signature bond. He recently relocated from Cadott to Withee. As terms of his release, Witmer cannot access the internet or be in contact with juveniles, including driving them around.
In 2012, Witmer was convicted of second-degree sexual assault of a child. He was sentenced in 2013 to serve 18 months in prison and placed on extended supervision for 8½ years. Department of Corrections records show he was released from Racine Correctional Institution in 2016.
According to the criminal complaint in Dane County Court, Witmer talked to a boy in an online chat room for gay teens. He arranged to meet the teen at a motel in Madison, where he assaulted the boy. He lived in Owen at the time of the offense.
Witmer had been a pastor at the Church of the Brethren in Stanley until 2011, then later worked at a Christian book distributor.
The new criminal complaint in Chippewa County Court states that Witmer had opened a Facebook page and was posting on the account, which is a violation of the terms of his sex offender registration status. Witmer was living in Cadott at that time.
